# Somani TV Player

This project builds a Windows x64 Electron installer named `SomaniTV-Player-Setup-1.0.0-x64.exe`.

## What this version does

- Installs as a Windows desktop app.
- On first launch, asks for the **published HTTPS URL** of your Somani TV web app and a
  **workspace activation key** (generated by the workspace owner in the portal).
- Confirms the workspace the key belongs to before continuing.
- Asks the customer to **name the player**; the workspace owner sees this name when approving.
- Shows the workspace's pre-existing screens in a dropdown; the customer picks one and presses
  **Activate Screen**. The player never creates screens; the screen must already exist in the portal.
- Creates a device-approval request with a 4-character verification code and waits while the
  workspace owner approves it in the portal (approval expires after 10 minutes).
- Stores the device token **encrypted with Windows DPAPI** (Electron `safeStorage`) in the
  player's application-data folder. The token is never written in plain text.
- After approval, playback runs in the embedded player at `<appUrl>/play`, reusing the tested
  paired-player web code. The encrypted token is injected into the page on every launch.
- Navigations are restricted to the configured app origin: the player window cannot follow
  links to other sites, and new windows are denied.
- F11 (or Esc) toggles full screen. F10 opens the setup screen.
- The web pairing-code journey (`<appUrl>/pair`) remains available as a fallback.

## Security notes

- The device token is stored only encrypted (DPAPI); the file is readable only by the user.
- Screens, pairing and revocation are enforced server-side; the token stops working as soon as
  the workspace owner revokes or replaces it.
- If the owner revokes the device, the player shows the pairing page. Press F10 and use
  "Unpair and start over" to clear the native token, then set up again with a fresh key.

## Not included in this version

Offline media caching, auto-update, licence-key offline validation, and native crash recovery.
Playback, heartbeats, media-link renewal and licence enforcement all come from the web player
and the server.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen may warn users. Do not install on production
displays until pairing, playback, unpairing, reboot behaviour, and licence enforcement have
been tested.

## Build locally on Windows

Install Node.js 22 LTS, then in this folder run:

```powershell
npm install
npm run dist:win
```

The installer appears in `dist/`.

## Build with GitHub Actions

1. In GitHub, open **Actions** > **Build Windows installer** > **Run workflow**.
2. Download the `SomaniTV-Player-Windows-x64` artifact from the completed run. The artifact is a
   ZIP containing the `.exe`.
3. Test the installer on a disposable Windows machine, then publish it as a GitHub Release.

## Configure the app

On first launch, enter the **published HTTPS origin** for Somani TV. Do not use a Base44
Preview URL. The app URL and chosen screen are stored in the user's Electron application-data
directory (`player-config.json`); the device token is stored encrypted (`device-token.bin`).
